claims.summary: For every 32-bit input, the sum_to export returns the sum of the natural numbers less than that input, represented in 32 bits.
claims.reason: The formal statement covers every 32-bit input and specifies the sum of all naturals below it, represented modulo 2^32, as intended.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.sumTo
claims.intent: `sum_to(n)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: `0 + 1 + … + (n − 1)`, wrapped to 32 bits.
details: Covers every 32-bit bit pattern for the single input, interpreted as an unsigned natural number from zero through the maximum 32-bit value.
The expected result is the sum of all natural numbers below the input, reduced modulo 2 to the 32nd power when represented as a 32-bit value.
Returns guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call in every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the expected value.

claims.summary: For every triple of 32-bit inputs, the clamp export returns the lower bound, upper bound, or input value selected by signed comparisons.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: The formal expression uses signed comparisons and returns the lower bound when x is below it, the upper bound when x exceeds it, and x otherwise, as intended—even when lo > hi.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: Covers every combination of three 32-bit inputs: the value, lower bound, and upper bound.
Both comparisons interpret the 32-bit values as signed integers. The result is one of the original input bit patterns, so there is no arithmetic wraparound in the selection.
Returns guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call in every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the selected value.
caveats: The comparison is signed, but the returned value is the original 32-bit bit pattern; the claim does not convert it to a signed result.
When the lower bound exceeds the upper bound, the nested comparisons still define a result, but the claim does not assert that it is a conventional clamp to a valid interval.

claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the gcd export returns their unsigned natural-number greatest common divisor as a 32-bit value.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: The statement covers all unsigned 32-bit input pairs and specifies their natural-number gcd; that result fits in 32 bits, matching the intent.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit bit patterns, interpreted as unsigned natural numbers.

The natural-number greatest common divisor is encoded as a 32-bit value; conversion to that width wraps modulo 2 to the 32nd power, although the natural-number result for these inputs fits in 32 bits.
Returns guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call in every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the expected value.
caveats: The inputs are converted to unsigned natural numbers before computing the greatest common divisor, so bit patterns with the high bit set are treated as large nonnegative values, not negative signed integers.
The claim does not assert any signed-integer greatest-common-divisor convention.
